citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The facility failed to have a complete Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) and has not had a site visit from the attending
veterinarian since 2024. The facility had only the first page of APHIS 7002 PVC form that lists the facility and attending
veterinarian.
A written Program of Veterinary Care that is current, facility-specific, and inclusive of all animal species maintained is
required to facilitate effective communication between the attending veterinarian and the facility. Failure to have a yearly
site visit from the attending veterinarian and an updated PVC completed in detail by the attending veterinarian prevents
APHIS officials from determining whether animals at the facility are receiving adequate veterinary care or whether
acceptable methods are being used to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat diseases and injuries.
Each dealer is required to employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements, and in the case of a part-time
attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary
care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises. Correct by July 09, 2026.

The facility failed to sanitize an outdoor enclosure housing two raccoons. The outdoor enclosure housing two raccoons
has a heavy buildup of brown greasy grime on the walls, shelves, wire mesh, and climbing structure. The wire mesh is
packed with hair, dirt, and debris, and the climbing structure is coated with grime, hair, and cobwebs. Although spot
cleaning occurs daily, surfaces are not being cleaned thoroughly or often enough to prevent this accumulation. A proper
sanitization system is needed to ensure regular, complete cleaning of all enclosure surfaces.
Sanitizing enclosures is essential to prevent the buildup of bacteria, parasites, and debris that can lead to disease, attract
pests, and create poor living conditions. Regular sanitization supports animal health, reduces stress, and ensures
compliance with required animal welfare standards.
Subsequent to the presence of an animal with an infectious or transmissible disease, cages, rooms, and hard-surfaced
pens or runs shall be sanitized either by washing them with hot water (180 F. at source) and soap or detergent, as in a
mechanical washer, or by washing all soiled surfaces with a detergent solution followed by a safe and effective
disinfectant, or by cleaning all soiled surfaces with saturated live steam under pressure. Pens or runs using gravel, sand,
or dirt, shall be sanitized when necessary as directed by the attending veterinarian. Correct by July 9, 2026.

citations.desc: Cleaning, sanitization, housekeeping, and pest control.
citations.narrative:
An indoor room housing three screech owl enclosures was not maintained in a clean, pest free condition. Fecal
droppings, old seed casings, dirt, and debris were present on the walls and flooring under all enclosures. A live roach was
observed under one enclosure, and spider webs were present beneath two enclosures.
Unsanitary conditions allow bacteria, fungi, and parasites to grow. Pests like roaches and rodents can carry pathogens
that increase the risk of illness in birds.
Premises where housing facilities are located, including buildings, surrounding grounds, and exhibit areas, must be kept
clean and in good repair in order to protect the birds from injury and disease, to facilitate the husbandry practices required
in this subpart, and to reduce or eliminate breeding and living areas for rodents, pests, and vermin. Premises must be
kept free of accumulations of trash, junk, waste products, and discarded matter. Weeds, grasses, and bushes must be
controlled so as to facilitate cleaning of the premises and pest control, and to protect the health and well-being of the
birds. Correct by July 9, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the facility representative.
